summary: 'Man shall not live on bread alone' — the first of three answers from Deuteronomy in the wilderness.
'Do not put the Lord your God to the test.'
'Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only.'
'You shall not murder' — the sixth commandment, first of the six 'you have heard... but I say' antitheses.
'You shall not commit adultery.'
The certificate of divorce.
'Do not break your oath' — a summary of Leviticus 19:12 and Numbers 30:2.
'Eye for eye and tooth for tooth' — the lex talionis (also Leviticus 24:20; Deuteronomy 19:21), which limited retaliation to equivalence.
'Love your neighbour.' The added 'and hate your enemy' is not in Leviticus; the Qumran Community Rule (1QS 1:9-10) does command hating 'the sons of darkness'.
'I desire mercy, not sacrifice' — quoted again at Matthew 12:7.
The Servant who will not break a bruised reed — Matthew's longest Old Testament quotation.
'Ever hearing but never understanding' — Isaiah's commission, on why Jesus teaches in parables.
'I will open My mouth in parables.'
'Honour your father and mother', with Exodus 21:17 on cursing parents.
'This people honours Me with their lips.'
'Male and female He created them', joined to Genesis 2:24, 'the two will become one flesh'.
'My house will be called a house of prayer' — combined with Jeremiah 7:11, 'a den of robbers'.
'From the lips of children and infants You have ordained praise.'
'I am the God of Abraham...' — the argument for resurrection from the tense of a verb.
The Shema's command to love God — the greatest commandment.
'Love your neighbour as yourself' — the second.
'The abomination of desolation' — also Daniel 11:31; 12:11; applied earlier to Antiochus IV in 1 Maccabees 1:54.
'Strike the shepherd, and the sheep will be scattered.'
'My God, my God, why have You forsaken me?' — quoted in Aramaic.
Mark opens with Malachi 3:1 and Isaiah 40:3 fused, attributed to Isaiah as the senior prophet.
'Hear, O Israel' — Mark alone includes the Shema's opening line.
Jesus reads Isaiah in the Nazareth synagogue and stops before 'the day of vengeance'.
John the Baptist applies Isaiah's 'voice' to himself.
'Not one of His bones will be broken' — the Passover lamb (also Psalm 34:20).
Peter's Pentecost text.
'The righteous will live by faith' — quoted again in Galatians 3:11 and Hebrews 10:38.
'Sit at My right hand' — Hebrews quotes Psalm 110 more than any other text.
'And to your seed' — Paul's argument from the singular noun.
The cornerstone in Zion, joined with Psalm 118:22 and Isaiah 8:14.
'The book of the genesis of…' — Matthew's opening phrase is the Septuagint's heading for Adam's line (and Genesis 2:4).
